sourceSentence: A simple line can land a punch in the final verse.
sourceMeaning: Have a strong impact; a fixed boxing metaphor.
reason: The guide uses a creative boxing image for a lyric line, but land a punch is established in learner dictionaries for actually hitting someone. The conventional reusable figurative expression for strong impact is pack a punch. Broadening land a punch across six assessed figurative contexts would teach a strained collocation and blur that distinction; switching the target to pack a punch would no longer teach the exact source expression. The source image is intelligible as a one-time comparison, but not a sound independent seven-step target at this checkpoint.

ownerBoundary: Selected owner488 punch above your weight concerns disproportionate achievement, not the impact of a line. This absence of a duplicate does not cure source-target naturalness.
sevenStepFeasibility: A single interpretive lesson on the source image is possible; six distinct, natural, target-bearing assessment decisions and two transferred writing models would require repeatedly extending a physical-hit collocation. Therefore no full Golden SOP draft was authored.
alternativesConsidered: Teach pack a punch: natural but violates exact-source target requirement.
Teach land a punch in literal boxing: natural but changes the guide source sense.
Teach creative metaphor as a one-time comparison: explain in source audit, not a separate seven-step unit.
mutations: None to draft, decisions, selected manifest or canonical owners.
